attempt.claim: Both pages render exactly the seeded facts, in a browser, against the real API. The calendar files every row under its own date soonest first - which the API cannot have handed it, because `GET /calendar-items` answers in name order and the seed's name order disagrees with its date order at every position - labels a deadline and a renewal differently, prints an amount only where one was recorded, and shows an undated row rather than dropping it. The task history lists every run newest first with its status, and each row links to `/tasks/<the seeded id>`, which is the detail slot s5 fills. Neither page shows another account's rows, and an account with nothing seeded gets the designed empty state on both. Finally, with the dashboard pointed at a port nothing is listening on, all three pages - watches, calendar and tasks - render their error state naming the cause, and draw normally again once the API is back. The outage half of that claim also proves the guard: with the API gone the middleware can no longer verify the session it is holding, and rather than bouncing the browser to a sign-in page that needs the same dead API to send a link, it lets the request through to the page that can say what happened. Nothing is disclosed by that, because every fact on every one of these pages arrives through the API that is not answering.

attempt.claim: Both pages render exactly the seeded facts, in a browser, against the real API. The calendar files every row under its own date soonest first - which the API cannot have handed it, because `GET /calendar-items` answers in name order and the seed's name order disagrees with its date order at every position - labels a deadline and a renewal differently, prints an amount only where one was recorded, and shows an undated row rather than dropping it. The task history lists every run newest first with its status, and each row links to `/tasks/<the seeded id>`, which is the detail slot s5 fills. Neither page shows another account's rows, and an account with nothing seeded gets the designed empty state on both. Finally, with the dashboard pointed at a port nothing is listening on, all three pages - watches, calendar and tasks - render their error state naming the cause, and draw normally again once the API is back. The outage half of that claim also proves the guard: with the API gone the middleware can no longer verify the session it is holding, and rather than bouncing the browser to a sign-in page that needs the same dead API to send a link, it lets the request through to the page that can say what happened. Nothing is disclosed by that, because every fact on every one of these pages arrives through the API that is not answering.

attempt.claim: An in-process dashboard compiles pages without opening a persistent cache, and takes its build directory with it when it stops. The cache is off for precisely the instances that could never read one back: `next.config.mjs` disables `experimental.turbopackFileSystemCacheForDev` when `NEXT_DIST_DIR` names a per-instance build directory, which is the test harness and nothing else - a real `next dev`, which has no such variable set, keeps its cache. With no writer left running there is nothing for teardown to race, so neither `Persisting is disabled for this session` - which is process-wide, and so was costing every later dev server in the same worker its caching - nor the panicking turbo-tasks thread behind it is reachable from this harness.
